definition.cn: “朝九晚五” 或 “平常的上班时间”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the standard working hours, from 9 AM to 5 PM, which are also the legally defined work hours. In modern society, "9-to-5" has become a fixed expression to describe a regular workday, indicating such a working routine and general schedule.

examples.en: She works a typical 9-to-5 job at an office.
examples.cn: 她在办公室做一份典型的朝九晚五的工作。

examples.en: I'm tired of the 9-to-5 grind and want a more flexible schedule.
examples.cn: 我厌倦了朝九晚五的枯燥生活，想要一个更灵活的时间安排。

examples.en: Not everyone is suited for a 9-to-5 routine.
examples.cn: 并不是所有人都适合朝九晚五的作息。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于标准的工作时间，即从上午 9 点到下午 5 点，这也是劳动法定时计工作时间。在现代社会，“9-to-5” 已经成为了描述一个常规工作日的固定表达，用以表示这样的工作常规和一般的工作时间安排。

definition.cn: “害群之马” 或 “一个有害的个体”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the old saying “one bad apple spoils the whole barrel,” illustrating that a negative or harmful individual can affect the entirety of their surroundings or group. In modern usage, "a bad apple" continues to signify someone or something that negatively impacts a group.

examples.en: It only takes a bad apple to ruin the entire team dynamic.
examples.cn: 只需一个害群之马就能破坏整个团队的氛围。

examples.en: They had to fire him because he was a bad apple disrupting the workplace harmony.
examples.cn: 他们不得不开除他，因为他是一个破坏职场和谐的害群之马。

examples.en: Be careful who you trust in this business, a bad apple can cause a lot of damage.
examples.cn: 在这个行业里，要小心信任谁，一个害群之马会造成很大的损害。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到一条古老的谚语 “一个烂苹果会把整篮苹果都弄坏”（One bad apple spoils the whole barrel）。这表明，一个负面或有害的个体可能会影响周围的人或整个群体。因此，在现代用法中，“a bad apple” 仍然用于指一个对群体有负面影响的人或事物。

definition.cn: “十三个”。这个短语用来表示数量时，比通常的一打（十二个）多一个。
definition.en: This phrase originates from medieval England. To avoid punishment for selling short-weight bread, bakers often gave an extra loaf to ensure they met the legal weight requirements. Hence, "baker's dozen" typically means thirteen.

examples.en: I ordered a dozen bagels, but the kind baker gave me a baker's dozen.
examples.cn: 我订了一打贝果，但是善良的面包师给了我十三个。

examples.en: With a baker's dozen of cookies, there's enough for everyone to have more than one.
examples.cn: 有十三块饼干，足够每个人多吃一块了。

examples.en: The bakery always includes an extra muffin, making it a baker's dozen.
examples.cn: 那家面包店总会多给一个松饼，使其成为十三个。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于中世纪的英格兰。为了避免因缺斤少两而受到惩罚，烘焙师在卖面包时常常会多给一个，以确保足够的分量。因此，“baker's dozen” 通常指的是十三个。

definition.cn: “大致的数字” 或 “粗略的估算”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the "ballpark" in American baseball games, which gives a sense of a broad but defined range. Over time, this term evolved to refer to an approximate or rough estimate. It is commonly used in situations requiring a quick judgment without the precision of detailed calculations.

examples.en: Can you give me a ballpark figure of the total cost?
examples.cn: 你能给我一个大致的总成本吗？

examples.en: Give me a ballpark figure and we'll refine it later.
examples.cn: 给我一个大致的数字，我们稍后再细化。

examples.en: I need a ballpark figure for how long this project will take.
examples.cn: 我需要一个这个项目大概需要多长时间的估计。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于美国棒球比赛中的 “球场”（ballpark），球场的面积给人一种宽泛但明确的范围感。后来，这个用语逐渐被用来表示粗略的或非精确的数字估计。通常在需要快速判断，但没有时间或数据进行精确计算的情况下使用这个表达。

title: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush

definition.cn: “手中之鸟胜过林中二鸟” 或 “稳妥之物胜过可能更多但不确定的事物”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from medieval hunters who believed that the game already caught is more valuable than potential game still in the bush. The phrase teaches people to appreciate what they have rather than risk it for something that might seem better but is not guaranteed.

examples.en: You should take the job offer; remember, a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
examples.cn: 你应该接受这个工作机会，记住，手中之鸟胜过林中二鸟。

examples.en: He decided not to sell his steady business in hopes of a bigger profit elsewhere, because a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
examples.cn: 他决定不卖掉自己稳定的业务去别处寻求更大的利润，因为稳妥之物胜过可能更多但不确定的事物。

examples.en: Considering the risks, she kept the guarantee in her pocket, knowing a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
examples.cn: 考虑到风险，她还是选择了保住已有的保障，因为手中之鸟胜过林中二鸟。

origin.cn: 这个成语起源于中世纪时期的猎人，他们认为已经抓在手里的猎物比还在灌木丛中的猎物更有价值。这句话用来教导人们珍惜已经拥有的东西，而不要冒险去追求那些可能更好但无法确定的东西。

definition.cn: “一点点” 或 “稍微”。
definition.en: This phrase is mainly used to emphasize a small degree of something and is a common colloquial expression. They can be used interchangeably without much difference. Usually, it is used to express a slight degree, or to indicate that the quantity or quality of something or someone is insufficient.

examples.en: I'm feeling a bit tired today.
examples.cn: 我今天感觉有点累。

examples.en: Can you please move a little bit to the left?
examples.cn: 你能稍微向左移动一点吗？

examples.en: She's a bit nervous about the interview.
examples.cn: 她对面试有点紧张。

origin.cn: 这个短语主要用于强调某事物的程度较小, 是一个常见的口语表达。它们可以互换使用，没有太大的区别。通常，用于表达程度比较轻微，或者表示某事物或某人的数量和品质不足。

definition.cn: “塞翁失马，焉知非福” 或 “因祸得福”。
definition.en: This phrase can be traced back to the 18th century. The literal meaning is a blessing that is disguised, suggesting that something that seems bad at first may ultimately result in something good. It highlights the idea that apparent misfortunes can sometimes lead to unexpected benefits.

examples.en: Losing that job was a blessing in disguise; it pushed me to start my own business.
examples.cn: 失去那份工作是塞翁失马，焉知非福；它促使我开办了自己的公司。

examples.en: Breaking up with her was really a blessing in disguise because she found someone even better.
examples.cn: 分手对她来说真的是因祸得福，因为她找到了一个更好的人。

examples.en: Failing that exam was a blessing in disguise; it made me realize I needed to change my study habits.
examples.cn: 考试不及格真是塞翁失马，焉知非福；它让我意识到我需要改变我的学习习惯。

origin.cn: 这个短语的来历可以追溯到 18 世纪。其字面意思是隐藏起来的祝福，意指一开始看起来是坏事，但最终却带来了好结果。这表明一些表面上的不幸事件实际上可能会导致更好的结果或意外的好处。

definition.cn: “有抱怨” 或 “有争执”。
definition.en: This phrase likely originates from the behavior of dogs fighting over a bone, where each dog shows great interest and a desire to claim it, resulting in a struggle. In modern context, it is used to describe when people have grievances or disputes that need to be addressed.

examples.en: I have a bone to pick with you about your comments yesterday.
examples.cn: 我对你昨天的评论有些不满，需要和你谈谈。

examples.en: She had a bone to pick with the manager regarding her last evaluation.
examples.cn: 她对经理上次的评价有些不满，需要讨论一下。

examples.en: They both have a bone to pick, so this meeting might be tense.
examples.cn: 他们两个都有不满需要解决，所以这次会议可能会很紧张。

origin.cn: 这个短语可能源自于狗之间争夺骨头的行为，其中每个狗都对骨头有极大的兴趣和争取的欲望，导致争斗。现代语境中，它用来形容人们之间有不满或争执的需要解决的问题。

definition.cn: “一缕新鲜空气” 或 “耳目一新”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from actual fresh air. When people are in a confined or stuffy environment, breathing in fresh air can make them feel comfortable and invigorated. This metaphor is often used to describe a person or thing that brings pleasure, a new perspective, or a refreshing change.

examples.en: Her innovative ideas were a breath of fresh air for the company.
examples.cn: 她的创新理念给公司带来了耳目一新的感觉。

examples.en: After months of routine work, the unexpected day off was like a breath of fresh air.
examples.cn: 经历了几个月的常规工作后，这次意外的休息日就像一缕新鲜空气。

examples.en: The new manager is a breath of fresh air; she's already made amazing improvements.
examples.cn: 新经理真是一缕新鲜空气，她已经做出了令人惊叹的改进。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于实际的新鲜空气，当人们置身于一个封闭或沉闷的环境中，突然吸入新鲜空气会令人感到舒适和振奋。这个比喻通常用来形容令人愉快、带来新鲜感或像是焕然一新的人或事物。

definition.cn: “一堆” 或 “许多”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the Old English word “bunc,” meaning a bundle or cluster. In modern English, "a bunch of" is widely used to refer to a large number of things, usually of the same kind. It is often used in informal contexts to indicate a considerable quantity.

examples.en: I bought a bunch of bananas at the market.
examples.cn: 我在市场上买了一堆香蕉。

examples.en: She has a bunch of friends coming over tonight.
examples.cn: 她今晚有一大堆朋友要来家里。

examples.en: There's a bunch of paperwork on my desk I need to finish.
examples.cn: 我的桌上有一堆文件需要处理。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到古英语单词 “bunc” ，表示一捆或一束。在现代英语中，“a bunch of” 被广泛使用，意思是指一大群的某种东西，通常是相同类型的事物。这个短语适用于非正式场合，常用来表示数量众多。

definition.cn: “心怀怨恨” 或 “积怨”。
definition.en: This idiom originated in 19th-century America, where people would place a small wooden chip on their shoulder and dare others to knock it off, signaling a readiness to fight. Over time, it has come to describe individuals who carry a grudge or are combative because of past experiences.

examples.en: He's always had a chip on his shoulder ever since he got passed over for the promotion.
examples.cn: 自从他晋升失败后，他一直心怀怨恨。

examples.en: You need to let go of the past and stop walking around with a chip on your shoulder.
examples.cn: 你需要放下过去，不要再对一切都心怀怨恨。

examples.en: She always seems to have a chip on her shoulder, ready to argue with anyone.
examples.cn: 她好像总是心怀怨气，准备和任何人争吵。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自19世纪的美国，当时有人会将一小片木屑（chip）放在自己的肩膀上，并敢于别人将其敲掉，以此行为表示自己愿意打架的准备。逐渐地，这个短语被引申为描述那些因为过去的经历而怀有怨气、易怒或好争的人。

title: A day late and a dollar short

definition.cn: “为时已晚” 或 “错失良机”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the 19th century in America, describing someone who is overly procrastinating, ultimately missing out not just on time but also on financial opportunities. It somewhat resembles Chinese idioms like “追悔莫及” or “亡羊补牢为时已晚”.

examples.en: He tried to submit his application, but it was a day late and a dollar short.
examples.cn: 他试图提交申请，但已经为时已晚。

examples.en: Her apology felt a day late and a dollar short after the damage was already done.
examples.cn: 在损害已经造成后，她的道歉显得为时已晚。

examples.en: The sale ended yesterday, so your interest now is a day late and a dollar short.
examples.cn: 促销昨天就结束了，所以你现在才感兴趣已经为时已晚。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于 19 世纪的美国，形容某人做事过于拖延，结果不仅在时间上晚了一步，而且经济上也没能因此赚到钱。有点类似于中文的 “追悔莫及” 或 “亡羊补牢为时已晚” 的意思。

definition.cn: “非常普通” 或 “随处可见”。这表示某事物极为常见，并没有特别的价值。
definition.en: This phrase originates from 19th-century America, where people could buy a dozen (12) of some cheap, common items like eggs or apples for a dime (10 cents). Over time, the phrase evolved to describe something that is very common and has little to no unique value.

examples.en: Cheap souvenirs are a dime a dozen at the tourist market.
examples.cn: 在旅游市场上，廉价纪念品非常普通。

examples.en: Local coffee shops are a dime a dozen in that neighborhood.
examples.cn: 在那个社区，当地咖啡店随处可见。

examples.en: Talent like his doesn’t come a dime a dozen.
examples.cn: 像他这样的天赋是很稀有的。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于 19 世纪美国，当时人们可以用 10 美分买到一打（12 个）某些廉价常见的商品如鸡蛋、苹果等。因此这个短语逐渐衍生出形容某物非常常见，毫无特别价值的意思。

definition.cn: “非同寻常的事物” 或 “极具挑战的事情”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in early 20th-century American slang, initially used to describe something that stood out or was extraordinary. The exact origin is unclear, but it is widely believed to come from the nickname of the "Duesenberg" car, which was considered particularly luxurious and excellent at the time. As a result, "doozy" became a term for anything exceptionally outstanding. In modern English, "doozy" often describes something remarkably good, unique, or extremely challenging.

examples.en: That test was a real doozy—one of the hardest I've ever taken.
examples.cn: 那个考试真是一个大挑战——是我参加过最难的之一。

examples.en: The storm we had last night was a doozy; it knocked out the power!
examples.cn: 昨晚的暴风雨真是非同寻常；它造成了停电！

examples.en: Be prepared for a doozy of a meeting tomorrow; we have a lot to discuss.
examples.cn: 准备好迎接明天的艰难会议吧；我们有很多事情要讨论。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于20世纪初的美国俚语，最初用于描述某事物极其突出或不同寻常。虽然具体的来源尚不明确，但普遍认为可能来自于 “Duesenberg” 汽车的昵称，这种车在当时被认为是特别豪华且杰出的，因此 “doozy” 也被用来形容任何特别杰出的事物。在现代英语中，“doozy” 通常用来描述某事物非常出色、独特，或是极具挑战和难度。

definition.cn: “多疑的托马斯” 或 “怀疑一切的人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the story in the Bible (John 20:24-29), where the disciple Thomas doubted Jesus' resurrection until he saw and touched Jesus' wounds himself. Hence, "a doubting Thomas" is used to describe someone who is skeptical and does not easily believe others or things.

examples.en: He's such a doubting Thomas, always needing proof before he believes anything we say.
examples.cn: 他真是一个多疑的托马斯，总是需要证据才能相信我们说的任何话。

examples.en: Don't be a doubting Thomas, trust me on this plan. It's going to work.
examples.cn: 不要做一个多疑的托马斯，相信我这个计划，它会成功的。

examples.en: My brother is a real doubting Thomas – he never takes anything at face value.
examples.cn: 我哥哥真是个多疑的托马斯，他从不轻信任何事情。

origin.cn: 该短语来源于《圣经·约翰福音》中的故事。门徒托马斯对耶稣复活表示怀疑，直到亲眼见到并触摸到耶稣的伤痕才相信。因此，“a doubting Thomas” 被用来形容那些总是怀疑或不轻易相信他人或事情的人。

definition.cn: “与（某事物）大不相同” 或 “远远不同”。
definition.en: This idiom dates back to 19th-century England, where it originally referred to the great distance between two places. Over time, it evolved to describe differences and distinctions. Nowadays, this phrase is commonly used to indicate a significant difference or a stark contrast between two things.

examples.en: Living in the city is a far cry from living in the countryside.
examples.cn: 住在城市和住在乡村大不相同。

examples.en: Her current job is a far cry from what she imagined herself doing after graduation.
examples.cn: 她现在的工作和她毕业后想象的工作大不相同。

examples.en: The new restaurant's food is a far cry from their old one.
examples.cn: 这家新餐馆的食物与他们之前那家的食物大不相同。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于19世纪的英国，最早用来表示从一个地方到另一个地方的距离非常远。后来，它被用于形容差异和不同。如今，这个表达常常用来形容两件事物之间有显著的差别或完全不一样。

definition.cn: “多余的人” 或 “不必要的存在”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the time of horse-drawn carriages, which typically had four wheels. A fifth wheel was unnecessary and had no function. In modern context, the phrase is used to describe someone who feels out of place or unnecessary in a group, much like an unneeded fifth wheel.

examples.en: I felt like a fifth wheel at their party since I didn't know anyone.
examples.cn: 在他们的派对上，我感觉自己像个多余的人，因为我不认识任何人。

examples.en: Whenever my friends go out on dates, I always feel like a fifth wheel.
examples.cn: 每当我的朋友们出去约会时，我总感觉自己像个多余的存在。

examples.en: Don't worry about becoming a fifth wheel at the family gathering; everyone will make you feel welcome.
examples.cn: 不用担心在家庭聚会上成为多余的人，大家都会让你感觉受欢迎的。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于以前马车时代。车子通常都有四个轮子，而第五个轮子是多余的，不起作用。在现代社会中，这个短语用来形容在一个团体里多余、无关紧要的人，就像多余的第五个轮子一样没有用处。

definition.cn: “昙花一现”，形容某事物或人曾经一度辉煌或成功，然而很快就消失了，并没有持久的影响力。
definition.en: This phrase originates from 18th-century flintlock muskets. These firearms would sometimes have the gunpowder ignite ("flash") without the bullet actually being fired ("in the pan" mechanism). Over time, the phrase came to describe any brief, fleeting success or occurrence.

examples.en: His performance was impressive, but it turned out to be just a flash in the pan.
examples.cn: 他的表演令人印象深刻，但结果只是昙花一现。

examples.en: The new product was selling well initially, but it proved to be a flash in the pan.
examples.cn: 新产品一开始卖得很好，但证明只是昙花一现。

examples.en: Many startups turn out to be a flash in the pan.
examples.cn: 许多创业公司最终都成了昙花一现。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于18世纪的火枪技术。当时的火枪用火药射击，有时候点火却未能成功发射，这就称为 "a flash in the pan"。后来，这个短语被用来描述任何短暂现象或昙花一现的成功。

title: A fool and his money are easily parted

definition.cn: “傻瓜和他的钱财很容易分离” 或 “愚人财难留”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the Bible, specifically the Book of Proverbs in the Old Testament. Since its inception, this proverb has been used to describe people who lack the ability to manage their finances or spend their money unwisely, resulting in their money quickly being depleted. In practice, it's often used to caution someone to manage their money wisely, or they risk losing it.

examples.en: He spent all his savings on lottery tickets. A fool and his money are easily parted.
examples.cn: 他把所有的积蓄都花在买彩票上了。愚人财难留。

examples.en: Buying unnecessary gadgets can drain your funds quickly. After all, a fool and his money are easily parted.
examples.cn: 购买不必要的小玩意儿会迅速耗尽你的资金。毕竟，愚人财难留。

examples.en: He invested in a dubious scheme and lost it all. True to the saying, a fool and his money are easily parted.
examples.cn: 他投资了一个可疑的计划，结果全都亏了。真如那句老话说的，愚人财难留。

origin.cn: 这个短语出自《圣经》中的《旧约‧箴言》。自从其出现以来，这个谚语一直用来形容那些缺乏理财能力或不明智地花钱的人，他们的钱很快就会被耗光。实际上，它经常被用来警告某人要明智地管理他们的钱财，否则他们很可能会失去它。

definition.cn: “努力加分” 或 “表扬你努力的精神”。
definition.en: This phrase comes from the grading system, where even if the actual performance is not outstanding, the effort and spirit shown can still earn a high evaluation. Used in colloquial speech, it typically indicates that even though someone's efforts didn't result in great success, their hard work should still be acknowledged and praised.

examples.en: You might not have won, but you definitely get an A for effort.
examples.cn: 你虽然没有赢，但肯定能得到一个 “努力加分”。

examples.en: The project didn't work out as planned, but the team deserves an A for effort.
examples.cn: 虽然项目没有按计划进行，但团队值得一个 “努力加分”。

examples.en: Her dance performance wasn't perfect, but she'd still get an A for effort from the judges.
examples.cn: 她的舞蹈表演不完美，但评委们还是会给她一个 “努力加分”。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于评分制度中的一个概念，即便考试成绩本身并不突出，但因其表现出努力的态度或精神，依然可以得到较高的评价。用在口语中，通常表示虽然某人的努力没有产生出色的结果，但他们的付出和努力应该被认可和表扬。

definition.cn: “人生的十字路口” 或 “关键抉择的时刻”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the image of a literal fork in a road where a single path splits into two or more directions, requiring a choice of which way to go. It is often used metaphorically to describe a critical decision point in one's life, where the choice made will have significant future consequences.

examples.en: During his mid-30s, he encountered a fork in the road with his career.
examples.cn: 在他三十多岁时，他的职业生涯遇到了一个关键的抉择时刻。

examples.en: Graduating from college presents a major fork in the road for many students.
examples.cn: 大学毕业对许多学生来说是一个人生的重要转折点。

examples.en: When the company restructured, she found herself at a fork in the road in her professional life.
examples.cn: 当公司重组时，她发现自己的职业生涯走到了一个关键的十字路口。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于道路分叉的情景，就像一条路分成两条或多条支路，需要选择前进方向。它常被用来比喻人生中的重要时刻，需要做出重大决定，这个决定会对未来产生深远影响。

definition.cn: “乐善好施者” 或 “好撒玛利亚人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a story in the Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke. In the story, a Samaritan helps a Jewish man who was attacked by robbers, despite historical animosity between Samaritans and Jews. Nowadays, it refers to people who selflessly help others.

examples.en: A good Samaritan reached out to help the elderly man who had fallen on the sidewalk.
examples.cn: 一位乐善好施者伸出援手，帮助了在人行道上摔倒的老人。

examples.en: She was a good Samaritan when she took the lost child to the police station.
examples.cn: 她把迷路的孩子带到警察局时，表现得像一位好撒玛利亚人。

examples.en: The anonymous good Samaritan donated money to help rebuild the community center.
examples.cn: 这位匿名的乐善好施者捐款帮助重建社区中心。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于《圣经》中的《路加福音》一则故事。在故事中，一位撒玛利亚人帮助了被强盗袭击的犹太人，尽管撒玛利亚人和犹太人之间存在历史上的敌对关系。这个短语现在用来指那些不求回报地帮助他人的善良人。

definition.cn: “心结” 或 “心理障碍”。
definition.en: Originally, this phrase came from the action of hanging up a telephone. Over time, it evolved to describe psychological obstacles or issues that a person can't easily get over. It's commonly used to talk about someone's fears, anxieties, embarrassments, or other negative emotional reactions.

examples.en: She has a real hang-up about speaking in public.
examples.cn: 她对公开演讲有真正的心结。

examples.en: He couldn’t enjoy the trip because of his hang-up about flying.
examples.cn: 由于对飞行的心理障碍，他无法享受这次旅行。

examples.en: I don't know why she has such a hang-up about talking to strangers.
examples.cn: 我不知道为什么她对与陌生人交谈有这样的心结。

origin.cn: 这个短语最早起源于电话的挂断 (hang up)，经过演变，它逐渐用来描述那种让人无法摆脱的心理障碍或困扰。通常用于描述一个人心中的恐惧、焦虑、尴尬或其他负面的情绪反应。

definition.cn: “难题” 或 “棘手的事情”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from hard nuts, which are difficult to open or crack. It is used as a metaphor to describe a problem or situation that is complex and requires considerable effort and time to solve. In everyday life, this expression is widely used to talk about challenges that need more intelligence or skill to tackle.

examples.en: The math problem was a hard nut to crack, but she finally solved it.
examples.cn: 那道数学题目是个难题，但她终于解决了。

examples.en: Negotiating with him is always a hard nut to crack.
examples.cn: 与他谈判总是很棘手。

examples.en: Finding an affordable apartment in the city is a hard nut to crack.
examples.cn: 在城里找到一个负担得起的公寓是一件棘手的事情。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于坚硬的坚果，它们很难打开或破解。用来比喻一个问题或情况很复杂，需要花费很多努力和时间才能解决。在日常生活中，这个表达被广泛用于描述那些需要更多智慧或技巧来对待的挑战。

definition.cn: “烫手山芋”。
definition.en: This phrase originated from the idea of holding a hot potato, which, if held in hand, would be very hot and difficult to hold without getting burned, prompting you to pass it on quickly. In English, it metaphorically describes issues or topics that are difficult to handle, causing embarrassment or controversy.

examples.en: The issue of rising taxes has become a hot potato for the government.
examples.cn: 税收上涨问题已经变成了政府的烫手山芋。

examples.en: The CEO's resignation turned into a hot potato during the board meeting.
examples.cn: 在董事会会议上，CEO 的辞职变成了一个烫手山芋。

examples.en: Nobody wants to discuss the hot potato of job cuts right now.
examples.cn: 现在没有人愿意讨论裁员这个烫手山芋。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自拿着烫热的土豆，如果你拿在手里会非常烫，很难保持不被烫伤，所以你得快速传递出去。在英语中，它形象地表示那些难以处理、令人尴尬或有争议的问题或话题。因为这些问题很麻烦，让人很难轻松应对，所以比喻为 “烫手山芋”。

definition.cn: “回扣” 或 “非法佣金”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the business or political realm. In these fields, "kickback" is often used to denote an illegal or unethical payment, usually given in return for awarding a contract, a purchase order, or other business transactions. Such kickbacks involve a transfer of benefits that undermines fair competition principles.

examples.en: The contractor was arrested for offering a kickback to secure the project.
examples.cn: 那位承包商因提供回扣来获取项目而被逮捕。

examples.en: He received a kickback from the supplier to ensure the deal went through.
examples.cn: 他从供应商那里收到了回扣，以确保交易顺利完成。

examples.en: They uncovered a series of kickback schemes within the company.
examples.cn: 他们揭露了公司内部一系列的回扣计划。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于商业或政治领域。在这些领域中，“kickback” 常用来表示一种非法或不道德的资金回报，其形式通常是给予承包合同、采购订单或其他商业交易中的回扣。这种回扣涉及利益输送，破坏了公平竞争的原则。

definition.cn: “有小道消息告诉我” 或 “我听说”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from old Western folklore, where birds were often seen as messengers. Particularly during the Victorian era, birds were symbolically used to represent the conveyance of news, signifying that the source of the information is unspecified or that the speaker does not want to disclose it, adding a touch of mystique.

examples.en: A little bird told me you're getting a promotion soon.
examples.cn: 有小道消息告诉我你很快会升职。

examples.en: A little bird told me that you have a new hobby.
examples.cn: 有小道消息告诉我你有了一个新的爱好。

examples.en: Guess what? A little bird told me you're getting married!
examples.cn: 你猜怎么着？有小道消息告诉我你要结婚了！

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于古老的西方民间传说，传说鸟儿会传递消息。尤其是在维多利亚时代，人们常常用鸟儿比喻小道消息的传播者，表示消息来源不明确或不愿透露具体的消息来源，带有一点神秘感。

title: A little learning is a dangerous thing

definition.cn: “一知半解是危险的。”
definition.en: This phrase originates from Alexander Pope's poem "An Essay on Criticism." In the poem, Pope argues that a small amount of knowledge can be more dangerous than complete ignorance, as it may lead people to become overconfident and make erroneous judgments and decisions. Hence, this idiom is often used to caution those who, due to their incomplete understanding, are prone to misunderstandings or hasty conclusions.

examples.en: He tried to fix the car himself, but a little learning is a dangerous thing—now it's in worse condition.
examples.cn: 他试图自己修理汽车，但一知半解是危险的，现在汽车情况更糟了。

examples.en: Before making any major decisions based on what you read online, remember that a little learning is a dangerous thing.
examples.cn: 在根据网上读到的内容做任何重大决策之前，记住，一知半解是危险的。

examples.en: A little learning is a dangerous thing—it's better to seek professional advice.
examples.cn: 一知半解是危险的——最好寻求专业建议。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于亚历山大·蒲柏（Alexander Pope）的诗《论批评》（An Essay on Criticism）。在诗中，蒲柏指出，只有一点点学习反而比没有学习更危险，因为它可能导致人们自以为是，做出错误的判断和决定。因此，这个短语通常用来警告那些由于掌握的不完全知识而容易产生误解或未经过深思熟虑的人。

definition.cn: “像筛子一样的记忆” 或 “记性差”。
definition.en: This idiom compares someone's memory to a sieve, implying that they have a poor memory. Just as a sieve cannot retain small particles and lets most things fall through, a person with a "memory like a sieve" tends to forget information easily. This idiom is commonly used to describe people who are forgetful.

examples.en: My mom has a memory like a sieve and keeps forgetting where she put her keys.
examples.cn: 我妈妈记性很差，总是忘记她把钥匙放在哪里。

examples.en: If you have a memory like a sieve, you might need to write things down more often.
examples.cn: 如果你记性不好，可能需要更频繁地把事情写下来。

examples.en: I've got a memory like a sieve these days; I can't even remember my own phone number.
examples.cn: 我最近记性很差，连自己的电话号码都记不住。

origin.cn: 这个短语比喻一个人记性很差，就像筛子无法保存细小的东西一样，信息也总是 “漏掉”。这来自于筛子的特性，筛子会让大部分东西通过，仅留下很少部分。在日常生活中，这个短语常用于形容那些容易忘事的人。

definition.cn: “透露一下你的想法” 或 “说说你在想什么”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the 16th century, used to ask someone what they were thinking. At that time, a penny, though not highly valuable, was enough to solicit someone's thoughts. Nowadays, this idiom is commonly used to express interest or curiosity about what someone else is thinking.

examples.en: You've been awfully quiet. A penny for your thoughts?
examples.cn: 你一直很安静。告诉我你在想什么好吗？

examples.en: A penny for your thoughts, Sam. You seem deep in thought.
examples.cn: 山姆，说说你在想什么吧。你看起来在深思熟虑。

examples.en: A penny for your thoughts. What's bothering you?
examples.cn: 告诉我你在想什么吧。是什么让你心烦意乱？

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于16世纪，用来询问别人正在思考什么。当时，一分钱虽然价值不高，但也足够换取对方的一点想法。如今，这个短语常用来表达对他人想法的兴趣或好奇心。

title: A penny saved is a penny earned

definition.cn: “省一分是一分” 或 “节约即赚钱”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a 17th-century proverb and is often credited to Benjamin Franklin. It emphasizes the importance of saving and frugality, conveying the idea that saving money is as valuable as earning it. In modern society, this expression is used to encourage people to save resources and money in order to achieve financial stability and accumulate wealth.

examples.en: My grandma always says, "A penny saved is a penny earned," whenever I spend money recklessly.
examples.cn: 每当我乱花钱时，我奶奶总是说 “省一分是一分”。

examples.en: You don't need that expensive gadget. Remember: A penny saved is a penny earned.
examples.cn: 你不需要那个昂贵的装置。记住：“节约即赚钱”。

examples.en: By making your coffee at home instead of buying it, you’re proving that a penny saved is a penny earned.
examples.cn: 自己在家里煮咖啡而不是买，你这个行为表明了 “节约即赚钱”。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于17世纪的谚语，通常被认为是由本杰明·富兰克林（Benjamin Franklin）普及的。它强调了储蓄和节约的重要性，表达了通过节约来积累财富的理念。在现代社会，这个表达可以用于鼓励人们节约资源和金钱，以达到经济稳定和增加财富的目的。

definition.cn: “完美风暴” 或 “多事之秋”。
definition.en: The phrase originates from meteorology, describing a scenario where multiple weather conditions converge to create a particularly severe storm. It's commonly used to describe situations where various adverse factors come together, leading to an extremely bad or dangerous situation.

examples.en: The company's financial issues, combined with the economic downturn, created a perfect storm.
examples.cn: 公司的财务问题加上经济衰退，形成了一场完美风暴。

examples.en: With the heavy rain and high winds, it was a perfect storm for a disastrous flood.
examples.cn: 大雨和强风结合，简直是一场灾难性洪水的完美风暴。

examples.en: The combination of tight deadlines and unexpected technical issues created a perfect storm for the project team.
examples.cn: 紧迫的截止日期和意外的技术问题结合起来，对项目团队来说简直是一场完美风暴。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于气象学，描述多个气象条件同时出现，导致一场非常严重的风暴。这个短语通常用来形容许多不利因素同时发生，导致一种极其糟糕或危险的情况。

title: A picture is worth a thousand words

definition.cn: “一图胜千言” 或 “图胜于言”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from an ancient Chinese proverb "百闻不如一见" (seeing once is better than hearing a hundred times), which was introduced into English and gradually evolved into the present form. The saying means that images or visual effects often convey information and emotions more richly and straightforwardly than words. In modern society, this idiom is often used to emphasize that sometimes, a visual representation can be more impactful than a verbal description.

examples.en: She showed us the photos from her vacation because a picture is worth a thousand words.
examples.cn: 她给我们看了她度假的照片，因为一图胜千言。

examples.en: When making a presentation, remember that a picture is worth a thousand words.
examples.cn: 做演示时，请记住图片胜于言。

examples.en: The infographic helped everyone understand the data better because a picture is worth a thousand words.
examples.cn: 这张信息图帮助所有人更好地理解数据，因为一图胜千言。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于古代中国的一句成语 “百闻不如一见”，它被引入英语并逐渐演变为今天的形式。这句话的意思是，图片或视觉效果所传达的信息和情感往往比文字更丰富、更直观。现代社会中，这个短语常用于强调在某些时候，文字的描述可能无法与图片的直观表现相提并论。

definition.cn: “小菜一碟” 或 “非常容易的事情”。
definition.en: This idiom originated in the United States during the 1930s. At that time, people used “a piece of cake” to describe something as easy as eating a piece of cake. Over time, this phrase became popular and is now used to depict any task that is easy to accomplish.

examples.en: The math test was a piece of cake for her.
examples.cn: 那次数学测试对她来说简直小菜一碟。

examples.en: Fixing the bike was a piece of cake for him.
examples.cn: 修理那辆自行车对他来说非常容易。

examples.en: Making this dessert is a piece of cake if you follow the recipe.
examples.cn: 如果你按照食谱来做，这道甜点简直小菜一碟。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于20世纪30年代的美国。当时，人们常常用 “a piece of cake” 来形容某件事情像吃一块蛋糕一样容易。后来，这个短语逐渐流行起来，用来描述任何容易完成的任务。

definition.cn: “一缕阳光” 或 “带来希望的人或事物”。
definition.en: This phrase is often used to describe a person or thing that brings hope, joy, or warmth in times of trouble or difficulty, much like the sun's rays breaking through clouds on a gloomy day to bring light and hope.

examples.en: Her smile is like a ray of sunshine on a cloudy day.
examples.cn: 她的微笑像阴天里的一缕阳光。

examples.en: During my toughest times, his support was a ray of sunshine for me.
examples.cn: 在我最艰难的时刻，他的支持就是我的一缕阳光。

examples.en: The news of her recovery was a ray of sunshine for the whole family.
examples.cn: 她康复的消息对整个家庭来说是一缕阳光。

origin.cn: 这个短语常用于形容某个人或某件事物，在困境或者苦难中带来了希望、欢乐或温暖，就像在阴霾的日子里，阳光穿透云层带来希望的光芒一样。

definition.cn: “敲竹杠” 或 “宰人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from slang and means that the price of a product or service has been unfairly inflated, making the buyer feel cheated and exploited. It is often used to describe unfair deals or overpriced goods and services.

examples.en: The tickets to the concert were a total rip-off.
examples.cn: 那场演唱会的门票简直是敲竹杠。

examples.en: He felt the cost of the new phone was a rip-off.
examples.cn: 他觉得新手机的价格简直是宰人。

examples.en: Don’t go to that restaurant, it’s such a rip-off!
examples.cn: 别去那家餐厅，他们的价格太坑了！

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于俚语，表示某个商品或服务的价格被抬高到不合理的程度，从而使人感到自己被欺骗和剥削。它通常用来形容不公正的交易或价格过高的商品和服务。

definition.cn: “有颗螺丝松了” 或 “精神有些失常”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from mechanical devices where a loose screw means the machine cannot function properly. Similarly, if a person has "a screw loose," it metaphorically suggests their mental state is a bit off or they are acting unusually. In everyday conversations, this phrase is often used to describe someone acting strangely or eccentrically.

examples.en: I think he's got a screw loose for jumping into that freezing water.
examples.cn: 我觉得他跳进那个冰冷的水里真是有颗螺丝松了。

examples.en: Her neighbors believe she has a screw loose because she talks to her plants.
examples.cn: 她的邻居们认为她精神有些失常，因为她会跟植物说话。

examples.en: Sometimes I think my brother has a screw loose when he starts collecting weird things.
examples.cn: 有时候我觉得我哥哥精神有些失常，当他开始收集奇怪的东西的时候。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于机械装置中的螺丝，如果螺丝松了，机器就无法正常运行。同样地，如果人 “有颗螺丝松了”，比喻他们的精神状态不太正常或者举动有些怪异。在日常对话中，这个短语常用来形容某人行为反常或古怪。

definition.cn: “搞砸了” 或 “失误”。
definition.en: This phrase comes from "screw up," which literally means to over-tighten something, and figuratively means to mess something up badly. In everyday language, "a screwup" is often used to describe someone who has made a significant mistake or messed something up.

examples.en: That was a major screwup on his part.
examples.cn: 那是他犯的一个重大失误。

examples.en: We can't afford another screwup this time.
examples.cn: 这次我们不能再搞砸了。

examples.en: Every project has at least one screwup, but we learn from them.
examples.cn: 每个项目至少会有一次失误，但我们会从中学到东西。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于 “screw up”，字面意思是把某物拧得过头，引申为把事情搞得一团糟、做出巨大错误。在日常用语中， "a screwup" 常用于形容某人做了一个重大的错误或搞砸了一件事情。

title: A sledgehammer to crack a nut

definition.cn: “小题大做” 或 “大材小用”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the concept of using excessive force to solve a trivial problem. Like using a sledgehammer to crack a small nut, it exaggerates and unnecessarily wastes resources. It is used to describe taking overly strong or complex measures to deal with a simple issue.

examples.en: Bringing in a lawyer for this minor dispute is like using a sledgehammer to crack a nut.
examples.cn: 请律师来解决这个小纠纷简直是小题大做。

examples.en: Installing a full security system for such a small store seems like a sledgehammer to crack a nut.
examples.cn: 在这么小的店里安装全套安保系统感觉像是大材小用。

examples.en: Buying a huge SUV for driving around the city is a sledgehammer to crack a nut.
examples.cn: 在城市里开这么大的越野车简直是小题大做。

origin.cn: 这个成语源自于使用超出所需的过多力量来完成一个微不足道的任务。类似于用大榔头砸开一个小坚果，这不仅夸张且不必要，还会造成浪费。它用来形容采取过于强硬或复杂的措施来处理简单的问题。

definition.cn: “聪明的人” 或 “机灵的人”。
definition.en: This phrase is used to describe someone who is very intelligent, quick-witted, or astute. It is somewhat informal but very complimentary. The term "cookie" here does not refer to an actual cookie but is used as a colloquial term for a person, indicating cleverness and smartness.

examples.en: She's a real smart cookie and always finds a way to solve problems.
examples.cn: 她真是个非常聪明的人，总能找到解决问题的方法。

examples.en: You can't fool him; he's a smart cookie.
examples.cn: 你骗不了他，他可是个聪明的人。

examples.en: My daughter is such a smart cookie, she learned to read before she turned four.
examples.cn: 我女儿特别聪明，在四岁之前就学会了阅读。

origin.cn: 这个短语用来形容一个非常聪明、有头脑或者非常机敏的人。这个表达有点非正式，但却充满了赞赏。短语中的 “cookie” 并非指实际的饼干，而是作为对人的一种称呼，表达机智和聪慧。

definition.cn: “滚雪球效应”。
definition.en: The "snowball effect" refers to something that starts small but grows larger and larger, with its impact increasing over time. This phrase originates from the natural phenomenon where a ball of snow rolling down a hillside gathers more snow and becomes bigger. Initially, it was used to describe the rapid expansion of force or impact, but now it can refer to any cumulative growth or expansion.

examples.en: Once the rumor started, it created a snowball effect and spread quickly.
examples.cn: 一旦谣言开始，就产生了滚雪球效应，很快传播开来。

examples.en: Her small investment had a snowball effect, eventually leading to big profits.
examples.cn: 她的小投入产生了滚雪球效应，最终带来了巨大的利润。

examples.en: The project took off slowly, but then the snowball effect made it hugely successful.
examples.cn: 项目起初进展缓慢，但随后滚雪球效应使它取得了巨大的成功。

origin.cn: “滚雪球效应” 指的是某件事情像滚雪球一样越滚越大，影响范围越来越广。这个短语起源于雪在滚下山坡时越来越大的现象，最初是指堆叠的力量或影响会迅速扩大，现在也可以泛指任何形式的累积性增长或扩大。

definition.cn: “毫无机会” 或 “机会微乎其微”。
definition.en: This idiom uses the idea of a snowball surviving in the fires of hell to illustrate something nearly impossible. Just as a snowball would quickly melt in the inferno, so too does this phrase indicate extremely slim chances of success.

examples.en: Winning the lottery? That's like a snowball's chance in hell.
examples.cn: 中彩票？那简直是毫无希望的事。

examples.en: He doesn't have a snowball's chance in hell of passing that exam without studying.
examples.cn: 他不复习的话，根本不可能通过那场考试。

examples.en: There's a snowball's chance in hell that we'll finish this project on time.
examples.cn: 我们按时完成这个项目的机会微乎其微。

origin.cn: 这个成语用雪团（snowball）在地狱（hell）中存活的几率来比喻一件几乎不可能的事情。雪团在炎热的地狱中会迅速融化，因而表示成功的机会极小。

title: A stitch in time saves nine

definition.cn: “小洞不补，大洞吃苦” 或 “及时缝一针，省下九针”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a sewing metaphor, indicating that if a small tear in fabric is mended promptly, it can prevent the tear from becoming larger and thus save more sewing work later. In broader terms, it suggests that early intervention to address small issues avoids bigger problems and saves time and effort. Consequently, this idiom emphasizes the importance of addressing issues in a timely manner.

examples.en: I know it's a small leak, but remember, a stitch in time saves nine.
examples.cn: 我知道这只是一个小漏，但记住，小洞不补，大洞吃苦。

examples.en: Fix that flat tire now; a stitch in time saves nine.
examples.cn: 现在就修好那个泄气的轮胎吧，及时缝一针，省下九针。

examples.en: You should update the software immediately; a stitch in time saves nine.
examples.cn: 你应该立即更新软件，及时解决可以避免大麻烦。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于缝纫的比喻，意思是如果能及时处理小问题，就能防止小问题变成大麻烦，进而避免更多的工作和烦恼。在某种情况下，有效的早期干预可以节省时间和精力。因此，用这个成语来强调及时处理问题的重要性。

definition.cn: “一箭之遥” 或 “非常近的距离”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from ancient times when people used physical phenomena to describe distances due to the lack of modern measuring tools. “A stone's throw” originally meant the distance a stone could be thrown, typically indicating a very short distance within easy reach. In modern English, this phrase is still used to signify that something is very close by.

examples.en: The store is just a stone's throw from my house.
examples.cn: 这家商店离我家仅一箭之遥。

examples.en: Her office is a stone's throw away from the coffee shop.
examples.cn: 她的办公室离咖啡店非常近。

examples.en: We spent the weekend at a cottage a stone's throw from the beach.
examples.cn: 我们在离海滩非常近的小屋度过了周末。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于古代，当没有现代测量工具时，人们常用物理现象来描述距离。“A stone's throw” 原意为石头投掷的距离，通常表示非常近的距离，脚力范围内都可以轻松达到。在现代英语中，这个短语依然被用来表示某地或某物体距离很近。

definition.cn: “小题大做” 或 “夸张的小事”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from Britain and has been in use since the 18th century. It describes a storm in a small container, like a teacup, which couldn't possibly impact the outside world. Thus, it is used to signify an overreaction or unnecessary worry about minor matters.

examples.en: The argument between them was just a storm in a teacup; it was nothing serious.
examples.cn: 他们之间的争论不过是小题大做，根本没什么大不了的。

examples.en: Don't worry about that mistake; it's just a storm in a teacup.
examples.cn: 不用担心那个错误，那只是小题大做。

examples.en: The media is making a storm in a teacup out of this minor issue.
examples.cn: 媒体在这个小问题上小题大做。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于英国，自18世纪开始被使用，形容在一个小容器（如茶杯）中引发的风暴不可能对外界造成重大影响。因此，用它来表示人们对小事的过度反应或不必要的担忧。

definition.cn: “风暴正在酝酿” 或 “即将爆发的危机”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the observation of weather patterns; when a storm is approaching, dark clouds gather in the sky. Similarly, metaphorically, "a storm is brewing" is used to describe impending trouble or a crisis, often indicating that a tense atmosphere or situation is becoming increasingly uneasy.

examples.en: You could tell from their argument that a storm is brewing.
examples.cn: 从他们的争吵中你可以看出风暴正在酝酿。

examples.en: With the new policy changes, a storm is brewing among the employees.
examples.cn: 随着新政策的改变，员工中风暴正在酝酿。

examples.en: I have a bad feeling about this meeting; a storm is brewing.
examples.cn: 我对这次会议有种不祥的预感，风暴正在酝酿。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到观察天气的经验，当风暴即将来临时，天边会出现乌云密布的景象。同样，在比喻意义上，“a storm is brewing” 用来形容即将出现的问题或危机，通常是指紧张的气氛或局势变得越来越紧张的情况。

definition.cn: “万无一失/必定成功的方法”。
definition.en: The phrase "surefire" means absolutely reliable or guaranteed to succeed, and it can be traced back to situations where a particular strategy or method is sure to achieve the desired outcome. In modern English, when we say something is "a surefire way", it means that method is almost guaranteed to succeed or has a very high probability of success.

examples.en: Studying hard is a surefire way to improve your grades.
examples.cn: 努力学习是提高成绩的万无一失的方法。

examples.en: Exercise is a surefire way to boost your health.
examples.cn: 锻炼是增强健康的必定成功的方法。

examples.en: Telling the truth is a surefire way to build trust with others.
examples.cn: 说实话是建立信任的必定成功的方法。

origin.cn: 这个短语中的 “surefire” 意思是绝对可靠的或保证成功的，可以追溯到用来形容某种计谋或方法必定能达到预期效果的情况。 在现代英语中，当我们说某种方法是 “a surefire way” 时，意指这种方法几乎肯定会成功，或者有极高的成功率。

definition.cn: “爱吃甜食” 或 “有甜食癖好”。
definition.en: This phrase can be traced back to the 19th century, indicating a person's strong liking for sweet food. "Tooth" here is used metaphorically to refer to a craving or preference for sweets. Similar to the Chinese phrase "甜食癖好," "a sweet tooth" vividly describes one's fondness for sugary treats.

examples.en: She has a sweet tooth and never skips dessert.
examples.cn: 她有甜食癖好，从不跳过甜点。

examples.en: If you have a sweet tooth, you'll love this candy shop.
examples.cn: 如果你爱吃甜食，你会喜欢这家糖果店的。

examples.en: He's trying to cut down on sugar, but his sweet tooth makes it hard.
examples.cn: 他在努力减少糖分摄入，但他的甜食癖好让这变得很难。

origin.cn: 这个短语可以追溯到 19 世纪，表示一个人特别喜欢甜食。“Tooth” 在这里是一个比喻，指的是对甜食的偏爱或嗜好。与中文中的 “甜食癖好” 相似，“a sweet tooth” 形象地描绘出一个人对甜食的热爱。

definition.cn: “一场难分胜负的比赛” 或 “难以预测的局面”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the act of tossing a coin to decide the outcome, which involves flipping a coin into the air and observing how it lands. The result is completely random and unpredictable, so "a toss-up" is used to describe a situation where the outcome is uncertain and hard to predict.

examples.en: It's really a toss-up whether we'll get there on time.
examples.cn: 我们能否按时到达真的是难以预测。

examples.en: The game tonight is a toss-up, both teams are equally good.
examples.cn: 今晚的比赛难分胜负，双方球队实力相当。

examples.en: Who will win the election? At this point, it's a toss-up.
examples.cn: 现在谁能赢得选举？这个时候还很难说。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于掷硬币来决定胜负的行为，即将硬币抛向空中，然后观察它落地时是哪一面朝上。这种情况的结果是完全随机和不可预测的，因此 “a toss-up” 被用来形容一个结果不明确、难以预测的局面。

definition.cn: “心不在焉” 或 “健忘的”。
definition.en: This phrase is often used to describe a state of being inattentive or forgetful. "Absent" means "missing" or "not present," and "minded" comes from "mind," referring to one's intellect or thoughts. Combined, "absentminded" describes someone whose thoughts feel absent, i.e., not focused.

examples.en: He's always so absentminded; he forgot his keys again.
examples.cn: 他总是如此心不在焉；他又忘记带钥匙了。

examples.en: An absentminded professor might leave his notes at home.
examples.cn: 一位健忘的教授可能会把笔记落在家里。

examples.en: She seems absentminded these days, always lost in thought.
examples.cn: 她最近似乎总是心不在焉，总是在发呆。

origin.cn: 这个短语通常用来描述一个人思想不集中或忘事的状态。“Absent” 意为 “缺席” 或 “不在”，而 “minded” 则来自 “mind”，意思是 “心智” 或 “思想”。合起来，“absentminded” 描述的是一个人的心思仿佛 “缺席了”，，即他或她没有集中注意力。

definition.cn: “隐藏的王牌” 或 “秘密武器”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from poker. In some poker games, certain cards of the players are not revealed, known as "hole cards". If one of those hidden cards is an Ace, it's referred to as an "ace in the hole". Broadly, the idiom means having a hidden advantage or a secret strategy that can be used to turn a situation around at a critical moment.

examples.en: We thought we were losing, but we had an ace in the hole.
examples.cn: 我们以为要输了，但我们有一个隐藏的王牌。

examples.en: His experience in negotiating is his ace in the hole during business meetings.
examples.cn: 他在谈判方面的经验是他在商务会议上的秘密武器。

examples.en: The new product launch is our ace in the hole for increasing sales this quarter.
examples.cn: 新产品发布是我们本季度增加销售额的秘密武器。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于扑克游戏。在某些扑克游戏中，玩家的某些牌是不可见的 “hole cards”。如果这张隐蔽的牌是一张 “Ace”，就被称为 “ace in the hole”。在更广泛的用法中，这个短语表示拥有一个在关键时刻能扭转局势的秘密优势或策略。

definition.cn: “隐藏的王牌” 或 “秘密武器”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from card games, especially poker. In these games, a player might hide an ace (the highest-value card) up their sleeve to use it unexpectedly when needed. In modern life, the phrase is used to indicate that someone or some team has a hidden advantage or a secret weapon that can be used at a crucial moment.

examples.en: She always has an ace up her sleeve during negotiations.
examples.cn: 她在谈判中总是藏有一张王牌。

examples.en: He thought he had lost, but then he pulled an ace up his sleeve and won the game.
examples.cn: 他以为自己输了，但随后他使出了藏在袖子里的王牌，赢得了比赛。

examples.en: The team didn’t reveal their ace up their sleeve until the last minute.
examples.cn: 团队直到最后一刻才亮出他们的秘密武器。

origin.cn: 这个短语来自于纸牌游戏，特别是扑克。在这些游戏中，一个玩家如果在袖子里藏了一张王牌（最有价值的牌），当他需要时可以出其不意地使用。在现代生活中，这个表达用来表示某人或某团队有一个隐藏的优势或秘密武器，可以在关键时刻使用。

definition.cn: “致命弱点” 或 “薄弱环节”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from Greek mythology. Achilles was a Greek semi-god hero whose mother tried to make him invulnerable by dipping him in the magical River Styx. However, she held him by his heel, which did not get submerged and thus became his only vulnerable spot. In the Trojan War, Achilles was killed by an arrow to his heel, making "Achilles' heel" a fixed expression to denote a person's or thing's fatal weakness.

examples.en: Despite his success, his short temper is his Achilles' heel.
examples.cn: 尽管他很成功，但急躁的脾气是他的致命弱点。

examples.en: The software is great, but its security issues are its Achilles' heel.
examples.cn: 这款软件很棒，但安全问题是它的致命弱点。

examples.en: His gambling addiction was his Achilles' heel.
examples.cn: 他的赌瘾是他的致命弱点。

origin.cn: 这个成语来源于希腊神话。阿基里斯是古希腊半神英雄，他的母亲为了使他刀枪不入，将他浸在神奇的斯堤克斯河中。然而，她握住他的脚跟，而那部分没有被河水浸泡，成了他身体中唯一的弱点。在特洛伊战争中，阿基里斯被箭射中脚跟而死，因此 “Achilles' heel” 也成为了指代一个人或事物致命弱点的固定短语。

definition.cn: “严格考验” 或 “最终检验”。
definition.en: The "acid test" originates from the 19th century, where people used acidic solutions (often nitric acid) to test the purity of gold. If the metal passed this acidic test, it was considered genuine gold; otherwise, it was fake. Nowadays, this phrase is used to describe a final test or extreme situation to determine the validity, quality, or reliability of something or someone.

examples.en: The acid test for the new product will be how well it sells in the market.
examples.cn: 对于新产品的最终检验将是它在市场上的销售情况。

examples.en: Facing a crisis is often the acid test of true leadership.
examples.cn: 面对危机常常是真正领导能力的严峻考验。

examples.en: Launching the new app is the acid test for our development team's skills.
examples.cn: 发布新应用程序是对我们开发团队技能的终极检验。

origin.cn: “Acid test” 起源于19世纪，当时人们使用酸性试剂（通常是硝酸）来测试黄金的纯度。如果金属通过了这种酸性检验，它就被认为是真金，反之则是假货。今天，这个短语被用来描述一种最终测试或极端的情况，以检验某物、某事物或某人。

definition.cn: 全面的；普遍的；在所有方面。
definition.en: This phrase originates from horse racing terminology, referring to placing bets on all of the races. In modern English, it is widely used to signify something that affects all parts or members of a given area, field, or organization. It typically describes widespread changes, measures, or applications.

examples.en: The company announced a 10% salary increase across the board for all employees.
examples.cn: 公司宣布全体员工普遍加薪 10%。

examples.en: There will be budget cuts across the board next year.
examples.cn: 明年将全面削减预算。

examples.en: The new policy applies across the board regardless of seniority.
examples.cn: 新政策无论资历如何，适用于所有人。

origin.cn: “Across the board” 这个短语起源于赛马术语，指的是在所有的赛道上投注。但是，在现代英语中，它被广泛用于表示某个方面、领域或组织的所有部分或成员。通常用于描述普遍的变化，措施或应用。

definition.cn: “行动胜于言辞”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from 16th-century England, and it means that actions are a more powerful demonstration of one’s intentions and feelings than words. It reminds people not to rely solely on what others say but to look at what they do to truly understand their intentions.

examples.en: He keeps promising to help, but actions speak louder than words; so far, he hasn't done anything.
examples.cn: 他说了很多次要帮忙，但行动胜于言辞，到目前为止他什么都没做。

examples.en: She says she loves him, but since actions speak louder than words, she's planning a surprise for him this weekend.
examples.cn: 她说她爱他，但因为行动胜于言辞，她正在计划这个周末给他一个惊喜。

examples.en: In politics, actions speak louder than words; politicians need to show their commitment through their deeds.
examples.cn: 在政治中，行动胜于言辞：政治家需要通过他们的作为来展示他们的承诺。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于16世纪的英国，意指实际行动比言辞更能表达一个人的真实意图和感受。它提醒人们不要仅仅依赖言辞，而是要通过实际行动来证明自己。

definition.cn: “火上浇油” 或 “进一步激化矛盾”。
definition.en: This phrase literally means adding fuel to a fire, making it burn more intensely. In a metaphorical sense, "add fuel to the fire" means to make an already bad or tense situation worse. It's often used to describe someone’s actions or words that exacerbate a conflict or problem.

examples.en: His comments only added fuel to the fire during the argument.
examples.cn: 他的话只是在争论中火上浇油。

examples.en: Don't add fuel to the fire by getting involved in their dispute.
examples.cn: 不要插手他们的争执火上浇油。

examples.en: Her criticism added fuel to the fire and made the team more upset.
examples.cn: 她的批评火上浇油，让团队更加不安。

origin.cn: 这个短语字面上的意思是往火上添加燃料，从而让火烧得更旺。在比喻的用法中，“add fuel to the fire” 意味着让已经糟糕或紧张的局势变得更严重。这通常用来形容某人的言行使冲突或问题变得更加恶化。

definition.cn: “雪上加霜” 或 “伤口上撒盐”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the fables of Aesop, an ancient Roman storyteller. In one of his fables, a dog, having fallen and injured itself, is further kicked by a passerby when trying to get up. This saying vividly describes the situation of adding further trouble or insult to an already bad situation.

examples.en: After losing the game, the team's captain criticized the players, adding insult to injury.
examples.cn: 在输掉比赛之后，球队的队长还批评了队员们，真是雪上加霜。

examples.en: Getting a parking ticket at that moment really added insult to injury.
examples.cn: 在那个时候收到停车罚单真是伤口上撒盐。

examples.en: He was already having a bad day, and then to add insult to injury, he missed his bus.
examples.cn: 他已经过得很糟糕了，接着他还错过了公交车，真是雪上加霜。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到古罗马寓言作家伊索（Aesop）的寓言故事。在这个寓言中，一只狗因摔倒而受伤，当它试图起来时，又被一个行人踢了一脚。在此背景下，这个短语形象地描述了在已经糟糕的情况下又增加了新的困扰或屈辱。

definition.cn: “与时间赛跑” 或 “争分夺秒”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from timed events or races where participants need to complete their tasks within a set timeframe, essentially racing against the clock. In modern usage, it is widely used to describe the urgency of completing tasks within a limited period, indicating the need to hurry up.

examples.en: We are working against the clock to meet the project deadline.
examples.cn: 我们正争分夺秒地工作，以赶上项目的截止日期。

examples.en: The team was running against the clock to finish the building before the storm hit.
examples.cn: 团队正在争分夺秒地赶工，以在暴风雨来临前完成建筑。

examples.en: Trying to catch the last train, she was racing against the clock.
examples.cn: 为了赶上最后一班火车，她正在与时间赛跑。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于比赛或竞赛中的计时场景。在很多赛事中，选手们需要在规定的时间内完成任务，因此他们是在与时间赛跑。现代社会中，这个短语被广泛用于形容人们在有限的时间内需要完成的紧迫任务，表示要尽快完成某事。

definition.cn: “提前” 或 “超前”。
definition.en: This phrase is used to indicate that something is completed faster than originally planned or expected. It emphasizes the extra time gained, which can relate to daily schedules, project progress, or any task with a timeline.

examples.en: We finished the project ahead of schedule, so we can start the next phase early.
examples.cn: 我们提前完成了项目，所以可以提早开始下一个阶段。

examples.en: The flight arrived ahead of schedule by 20 minutes.
examples.cn: 航班提前20分钟到达。

examples.en: Thanks to everyone's hard work, we are ahead of schedule and might complete the task by tomorrow.
examples.cn: 多亏了大家的努力，我们超前了进度，可能明天就能完成任务。

origin.cn: 这个短语用于表示某事物比原计划或预计的时间更快地完成。它强调提前超出的时间，可能是日常安排、项目进行或任何有时间表的任务。

definition.cn: “雷声大，雨点小” 或 “虚张声势”。
definition.en: This idiom derives from the behavior of dogs that bark loudly but do not bite. It is used to describe people who speak in a threatening or aggressive manner but do not follow up with action or do not pose a real threat. It reflects verbal intimidation without corresponding actions or ability.

examples.en: Don't be afraid of him; he's all bark and no bite.
examples.cn: 别怕他；他就是雷声大，雨点小。

examples.en: She may threaten to call the police, but she's all bark and no bite.
examples.cn: 她可能会威胁叫警察，但她只是虚张声势。

examples.en: His threats are all bark and no bite, so don't worry too much about them.
examples.cn: 他的威胁只是雷声大，雨点小，所以别太担心。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于狗的行为，即只狂吠但不咬人。用来形容那些说话声势汹汹但实际上并不采取行动或没有实质威胁的人。这种表达方式反映了言辞上的威胁或吓唬，却缺乏实际的行动或能力。

definition.cn: “所有的打赌都作废了” 或 “情况不确定了，一切都难以预料”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from gambling; when the rules or circumstances change, all bets placed are canceled or recalculated. In everyday use, this idiom is used to indicate that the situation has changed, and previous expectations or promises can no longer be relied upon.

examples.en: Once the CEO resigned, all bets are off regarding the company's future.
examples.cn: 一旦 CEO 辞职，公司未来的情况就变得无法预料了。

examples.en: If it starts raining, all bets are off for the soccer game this afternoon.
examples.cn: 如果开始下雨了，今天下午的足球比赛就难说了。

examples.en: With the new law in place, all bets are off for the old business practices.
examples.cn: 有了新法律，旧的商业惯例就不一定能继续了。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于赌博，在赌博中，如果规则或情况发生了变化，所有的赌注都会被取消或重新计算。在日常使用中，这个短语被用来表示情况已经发生了变化，不能依赖先前的预期或承诺。

definition.cn: “我完全不懂” 或 “像天书一样难懂”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from Shakespeare's play "Julius Caesar," where a character named Casca says that something is as incomprehensible to him as Greek. Essentially, it is used to describe something that someone cannot understand, akin to hearing or seeing Greek, which is completely indecipherable to them. It's often used to refer to technical jargon, formulas, or other complex, hard-to-understand matters.

examples.en: All this technical jargon is all Greek to me.
examples.cn: 所有这些技术术语对我来说像天书一样难懂。

examples.en: When they started discussing quantum physics, it was all Greek to me.
examples.cn: 当他们开始讨论量子物理时，对我来说就像在听天书。

examples.en: I tried to read the legal document, but it was all Greek to me.
examples.cn: 我试图读那份法律文件，但对我来说完全看不懂。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自莎士比亚的戏剧《凯撒大帝》，其中角色塞拉尔引用到希腊语言对他来说完全陌生。本质上，它用来形容某人无法理解的事物，就像听到或看到希腊语一样完全无法理解。这种表达也经常用于技术术语、公式等难以理解的事物上。

definition.cn: “非常善良” 或 “心地很好”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the traditional view of the heart as the center of emotions, particularly in Western culture where the heart is often considered a symbol of love, compassion, and kindness. So, saying someone is "all heart" implies they are very kind, good-hearted, full of compassion and selflessness.

examples.en: She's all heart, always helping those in need.
examples.cn: 她心地很好，总是帮助那些需要帮助的人。

examples.en: You can tell he's all heart by the way he volunteers at the shelter.
examples.cn: 你可以从他在避难所做志愿者的方式看出他非常善良。

examples.en: Despite his tough exterior, he's really all heart.
examples.cn: 尽管他外表坚强，但他内心真的很善良。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于对心脏作为情感中心的传统看法，特别是在西方文化中，心脏常被认为是爱、慈悲和善良的象征。因此，说一个人是 "all heart" 意味着他们非常善良，心地很好，充满同情心和无私奉献的精神。

definition.cn: “同舟共济” 或 “处境相同”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the history of seafaring. If people on a boat face danger or problems, they must work together to solve them because they are "all in the same boat." In modern contexts, this idiom is used to indicate that everyone is in the same situation and must face and solve problems together.

examples.en: During the pandemic, we were all in the same boat, trying to adjust to new norms.
examples.cn: 在疫情期间，我们都处于相同的境遇，努力适应新的常态。

examples.en: We can't blame him; we're all in the same boat right now.
examples.cn: 我们不能责怪他；我们现在都处于同样的境遇。

examples.en: It’s comforting to know that we’re all in the same boat.
examples.cn: 知道大家都处于同样的境遇，让人感到宽慰。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于航海的历史。如果船上的人面临危险或遇到困境，他们必须共同努力去解决问题，因为他们都是 “同在一条船上”。在现代语境中，这个成语被用来表示大家处于相同的境遇，需要一起面对和解决问题。

definition.cn: “不开玩笑/言归正传”。
definition.en: This phrase is often used to emphasize that the following statement is serious or important. Even though the previous conversation may have been joking or light-hearted, saying this signals that the mood should now shift to a more serious tone.

examples.en: All kidding aside, we really need to focus and finish this project by Friday.
examples.cn: 不开玩笑，我们真的需要专注，争取在周五前完成这个项目。

examples.en: All kidding aside, I think you did an amazing job.
examples.cn: 言归正传，我认为你做得非常出色。

examples.en: All kidding aside, it's important to maintain a healthy lifestyle.
examples.cn: 不开玩笑，保持健康的生活方式是很重要的。

origin.cn: 这个短语常用于强调接下来的内容是认真的或重要的。虽然前面可能是在开玩笑、幽默轻松，但说这句话表示要撇开玩笑，开始严肃认真起来。

definition.cn: “到处都是” 或 “杂乱无章”。
definition.en: This phrase literally means "all over the places on the map." It's often used to indicate that something or someone is very scattered, unfocused, or lacking clear direction. It's commonly used to describe thoughts, conversations, or plans that are disorganized or lack structure.

examples.en: His ideas during the meeting were all over the map.
examples.cn: 他在会议上的想法杂乱无章。

examples.en: Her speech was all over the map, covering too many unrelated topics.
examples.cn: 她的演讲杂乱无章，涵盖了太多无关的主题。

examples.en: Our discussion was all over the map, and we couldn't reach a conclusion.
examples.cn: 我们的讨论杂乱无章，不能得出任何结论。

origin.cn: 这个短语字面上的意思是 “地图上的各处”。它常用来表示某事或某人十分分散、不集中或者没有清晰的方向。通常用于描述人的思维、谈话或计划混乱、没有条理。

definition.cn: “一切准备就绪” 或 “万事俱备”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from various scenarios in life, such as before traveling, meetings, or events, used to indicate that everything is in order and ready to go. It is widely used in both casual and formal situations to show that preparations are complete and things can proceed or start.

examples.en: We’re all set for the trip. Did you pack your bag?
examples.cn: 我们的旅行准备就绪。你把行李打包了吗？

examples.en: The team is all set for the presentation tomorrow.
examples.cn: 团队已经为明天的演示做好了准备。

examples.en: Dinner’s all set. Let's eat.
examples.cn: 晚餐准备就绪。我们开始吃吧。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于生活中的各种场景中，例如旅游、会议或活动之前，为了表示所有事情、物品已妥善完毕，准备工作已经完成。它广泛应用在各种日常和正式的情境中，指示准备工作已经完成，可以开始或继续接下来的活动。

definition.cn: 笨手笨脚，手指不灵活。
definition.en: This phrase dates back to the 19th century and refers to someone who is very clumsy or not dexterous with their hands. Imagine if a person's fingers were all thumbs; they would find it very difficult to perform tasks requiring fine motor skills. This is often used to describe someone who is particularly awkward or unskillful at certain tasks.

examples.en: I'm all thumbs when it comes to wrapping gifts.
examples.cn: 说到包礼物，我总是笨手笨脚的。

examples.en: He's all thumbs in the kitchen and always makes a mess.
examples.cn: 他在厨房里总是笨手笨脚的，总是搞得一团糟。

examples.en: I'm all thumbs when trying to put together IKEA furniture.
examples.cn: 我在组装宜家的家具时总是笨手笨脚的。

origin.cn: 这个短语的来源可以追溯到19世纪，指的是一个人非常不协调，无法灵活地使用手指。想象一个人所有的手指都是拇指，那么他在进行精细动作时将会显得非常笨拙。这通常用于描述那些在某些任务上显得特别不熟练或者笨拙的人。

definition.cn: “全错的” 或 “大错特错”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the 1920s American slang, where "all wet" was used to describe someone or something completely wrong or mistaken. The earliest uses might be related to popular humor and comedy scenes of the time, often portraying someone failing or being misunderstood, similar to being soaking wet.

examples.en: Your idea about skipping work to get ahead is all wet.
examples.cn: 你认为为了提前完成工作而翘班的想法是大错特错的。

examples.en: He's all wet if he thinks the boss will approve that plan.
examples.cn: 如果他认为老板会批准那个计划，那他就大错特错了。

examples.en: The theory that the Earth is flat is completely all wet.
examples.cn: 地球是平的这个理论完全是错的。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于20世纪20年代的美国俚语，当时 “all wet” 用于形容某人或者某事完全错误或者误会。最早的用法可能与当时流行的某些幽默剧以及喜剧场景有关，这些情景通常表现某人失败或误解，像落汤鸡一样（浑身湿透）。

definition.cn: “随波逐流” 或 “被带着走”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the scenario of joining a car ride, meaning participating in an activity without being genuinely involved or making decisions. It's often used to describe people who are being guided and do not take an active role, simply going along with the flow.

examples.en: I didn't really want to go to the party, but I went along for the ride.
examples.cn: 我其实并不想去参加那个派对，但还是随波逐流跟去了。

examples.en: He wasn't an active participant in the project; he was just along for the ride.
examples.cn: 他并没有积极参与这个项目，只是被带着走。

examples.en: She felt like she was just along for the ride in her friend's adventure.
examples.cn: 她觉得自己在朋友的冒险中只是随波逐流。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自乘车旅行的情景，意指参与某活动但并未真正投入或参与决策。常用来形容那些被牵引着行动的人，他们并没有主导权或深度参与，只是随大流。

definition.cn: “大转变” 或 “完全改变主意”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a military command used in drills, indicating for soldiers to quickly turn around and face the opposite direction. In everyday usage, it is used to describe a person making a complete 180-degree turn in their opinions, plans, or stance, essentially changing their mind or course of action entirely.

examples.en: After hearing the new evidence, the jury made an about-face in their decision.
examples.cn: 在听到新的证据后，陪审团在决定上来了个大转变。

examples.en: The company did an about-face on its policy after the customer backlash.
examples.cn: 在顾客强烈反对后，公司在政策上来了个彻底的改变。

examples.en: He made an about-face regarding his career path and decided to become a teacher.
examples.cn: 他在职业道路上发生了大转变，决定成为一名教师。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于军队操练中的命令，表示军人迅速转身，面向相反的方向。在日常生活中，它用来形容某人在观点、计划或立场上发生了180度的大转变，完全改变自己的想法或行动方向。

definition.cn: “肩上的负担” 或 “沉重的负担”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the narrative poem "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner" by English Romantic poet Samuel Taylor Coleridge. In the poem, a sailor kills an albatross, and his crewmates punish him by hanging the dead bird around his neck. This story symbolizes carrying a heavy burden or responsibility, thus evolving into the idiom for describing something that causes significant distress and is hard to get rid of.

examples.en: That old debt is an albatross around my neck.
examples.cn: 那笔旧债是我肩上的一个负担。

examples.en: His criminal record is an albatross around his neck, stopping him from getting a job.
examples.cn: 他的犯罪记录是他肩上的一个负担，让他找不到工作。

examples.en: The ongoing lawsuit has become an albatross around her neck.
examples.cn: 那起未了的诉讼案件成了她肩上的负担。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自英国浪漫主义诗人塞缪尔·泰勒·柯勒律治（Samuel Taylor Coleridge）的叙事诗《古舟子咏》（The Rime of the Ancient Mariner）。在诗中，一位水手杀死了一只信天翁（albatross），结果他的船员们将那只死鸟挂在他的脖子上作为惩罚。这个故事象征着背负着沉重的负担或责任的形象，从而演化为这个成语，用来描述让人感到困扰、难以摆脱的负担。

title: An apple a day keeps the doctor away

definition.cn: “一天一个苹果，医生远离我” 或者 “每日一苹果，医生远离我”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a 19th-century Welsh proverb: “Eat an apple on going to bed, and you’ll keep the doctor from earning his bread.” It emphasizes that regularly consuming fruits, especially apples, helps maintain good health and can reduce the frequency of visiting the doctor. This expression is often used to encourage people to develop the habit of eating fruits for better health.

examples.en: My grandma always says, "An apple a day keeps the doctor away."
examples.cn: 我奶奶总说：“每天一个苹果，医生远离我”。

examples.en: I try to eat more fruits because I believe in "an apple a day keeps the doctor away."
examples.cn: 我尝试多吃水果，因为我相信 “每日一个苹果，医生远离我”。

examples.en: You should include more apples in your diet. Remember, "an apple a day keeps the doctor away."
examples.cn: 你应该在饮食中添加更多的苹果。记住，“每天一个苹果，医生远离我”。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于19世纪的威尔士谚语 “Eat an apple on going to bed, and you’ll keep the doctor from earning his bread”。 它强调了经常食用水果，特别是苹果，有助于保持健康并减少去看医生的频率。这个表达经常被用来鼓励人们养成吃水果的好习惯，从而促进健康。

title: An old head on young shoulders

definition.cn: “年少老成” 或 “年纪轻轻却很有智慧”。
definition.en: The origin of this phrase comes from the appreciation of young individuals who show maturity and wisdom beyond their years. It is often used to describe someone young who demonstrates characteristics of being wise, experienced, or mature. This idiom has been widely used in the English-speaking world for centuries to describe young people who exhibit an extraordinary level of maturity when dealing with problems.

examples.en: Despite being only 12, she speaks with the wisdom of someone many years older, truly an old head on young shoulders.
examples.cn: 尽管她只有 12 岁，但她说话的智慧却像比她大很多岁的人，真是一位年少老成的人。

examples.en: He's an old head on young shoulders — always giving good advice beyond his years.
examples.cn: 他年纪轻轻却很老成——总是能给出超越他年龄的好建议。

examples.en: With her thoughtful insights, it's clear she’s an old head on young shoulders.
examples.cn: 通过她深思熟虑的见解，很明显她是个年少老成的人。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源源于对年轻人表现出超出其年纪的成熟和智慧的赞赏。通常用来形容一个年轻人尽管年纪轻轻，但却表现出了老练、成熟、甚至是经验丰富的特点。这个成语多个世纪以来在英语世界中被广泛使用，用来形容那些在处理问题时展现出无与伦比的成熟度的年轻人。

definition.cn: “老灵魂” 或 “心智成熟的人”。
definition.en: This phrase describes someone who is not tied to the contemporaneous cultural limitations and exhibits deep thoughts and maturity. Often, such individuals, even if young, display wisdom and insight that transcend their age. This expression actually praises these people for possessing maturity and depth of thought beyond their years.

examples.en: Though he is just a teenager, he is often described as an old soul because of his wisdom.
examples.cn: 虽然他只是个少年，但因为他的智慧，人们常称他为老灵魂。

examples.en: She loves vintage music and has the tastes of an old soul.
examples.cn: 她喜欢复古音乐，品味像一个老灵魂。

examples.en: His thoughtful and introspective nature makes everyone see him as an old soul.
examples.cn: 他的深思熟虑和自省的性格使每个人都觉得他是个老灵魂。

origin.cn: 这个短语用来描述那些不受当前时代文化所限定，有着深刻思维和成熟心智的人。通常，这样的人即使年轻也表现出与其年龄不符的智慧和洞见。这个表达实际上赞扬了这些人拥有超越年龄的成熟和思想深度。

definition.cn: “坦诚直率的人” 或 “毫无遮掩的人”。这个短语用于描述一个人对他自己的生活和情感非常坦率，毫无保留，如同展开一本书一般，可以让人轻易 “读取”。

examples.en: Jane is an open book; she never hides her feelings.
examples.cn: 简是个坦诚直率的人；她从不隐藏自己的感情。

examples.en: You don't need to guess what's on his mind, he's an open book.
examples.cn: 你不需要猜他在想什么，他是一个毫无遮掩的人。

examples.en: Unlike her sister, Sarah is an open book and shares everything about her life.
examples.cn: 与她的妹妹不同，莎拉是个坦诚的人，毫无保留地分享她的生活。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到书本提供信息和故事的方式。一本书，当被打开时，就可以被任何人阅读和理解。因此这个短语用了比喻，指的是那些以同样透明和公开的方式展示自己的人。

title: An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure

definition.cn: “一分预防胜过十分治疗” 或 “预防胜于治疗”。
definition.en: The literal meaning of this proverb is: an ounce of prevention is worth more than a pound of cure. The core idea is that taking preventative measures in advance can reduce the trouble and cost of dealing with issues later on. The idiom is believed to date back to ancient times, but it was popularized by Benjamin Franklin in the 18th century, especially in his speech about fire safety, emphasizing that preventing fires is much more important than dealing with the aftermath.

examples.en: She always follows the saying "an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure" by keeping her house well-maintained.
examples.cn: 她总是遵循 “预防胜于治疗” 的原则，保持房子的良好维护。

examples.en: Vaccinations are a great example of how an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.
examples.cn: 疫苗接种就是 “预防胜于治疗” 的一个很好的例子。

examples.en: By saving money regularly, he proves that an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure for financial stability.
examples.cn: 通过定期储蓄，他证明预防胜于治疗对于财务稳定性来讲是切实有效的。

origin.cn: 这个谚语的字面意思是：一盎司的预防比一磅的治疗更有价值。它的核心观念是提前采取预防措施可以减少之后处理问题的麻烦和成本。这个谚语的出现被认为可以追溯到古代，但是在18世纪，由本杰明·富兰克林特别在关于火灾安全的演讲中广泛传播。他提到，预防火灾的重要性远远大于事后补救。

definition.cn: “你在开玩笑吧？” 或 “你在逗我吗？”。
definition.en: This phrase is often used to express doubt, surprise, or disbelief at someone's statement or actions. In conversations, it serves as a way to question whether the other person is being serious or truthful.

examples.en: Are you kidding me? There's no way she finished that project in one day.
examples.cn: 你在开玩笑吧？她不可能在一天内完成那个项目。

examples.en: Are you kidding me? We just cleaned the house yesterday!
examples.cn: 你在逗我吗？我们昨天才打扫过房子！

examples.en: Are you kidding me? This car costs how much?
examples.cn: 你在开玩笑吧？这辆车要多少钱？

origin.cn: 这个短语常用于表达怀疑、惊讶或不相信某人的陈述或行为。在口语中，它是用来质疑对方所说的话是否认真或可信的一种方式。

definition.cn: “事后诸葛” 或 “舒适沙发上的指挥官”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from football, where the quarterback is a crucial position making calls on the field. The "armchair" symbolizes someone who is comfortable and not participating actively. Combined, the phrase metaphorically describes a person who offers opinions and criticisms after the event has taken place without having been involved in the decision-making or action.

examples.en: It's easy to be an armchair quarterback when you’re not the one making the tough decisions.
examples.cn: 当你不是做出艰难决定的人时，充当事后诸葛当然很容易。

examples.en: Don't be an armchair quarterback, help us find a solution.
examples.cn: 别当个事后诸葛了，帮我们找个解决方案吧。

examples.en: After the project failed, everyone became an armchair quarterback.
examples.cn: 项目失败后，人人都成了事后诸葛。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于美国橄榄球比赛中的 “四分卫” 角色。而 “armchair”（扶手椅）则象征着舒适、不参与实际行动的人。组合在一起，这个短语形象地描述了那些不参与实际操作，只是在事后评头论足的人。此短语在日常生活中常用来形容那些在履行完一个决定或行动后，用自己的 “高见” 来评判别人的人。

definition.cn: “全副武装” 或 “武装到牙齿”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from scenarios in battle or conflict, referring to someone who is fully equipped and armed to the utmost. In modern English, this idiom is often used to describe someone who is very well prepared for something, possibly extending beyond physical armament to mental readiness.

examples.en: The police officers were armed to the teeth during the raid.
examples.cn: 警察在突袭过程中全副武装。

examples.en: He entered the meeting armed to the teeth with data and reports.
examples.cn: 他带着各种数据和报告进入了会议，全副武装。

examples.en: The soldiers went into battle armed to the teeth.
examples.cn: 士兵们全副武装地投入战斗。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于战斗或冲突中的情景，指的是某人装备齐全，武器装备到极致。在现代英语中，这个成语常用来形容某人对某事物或任务准备得非常充分，可能不仅限于物质上的装备，还可以指精神上的准备。

definition.cn: “全天候” 或 “24 小时不停”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from describing an activity or service that continues non-stop throughout the entire 24-hour day, often used to indicate an effort, watch, or service happening during all periods of the day. It is typically applied in contexts like emergencies, medical services, or situations requiring constant attention, such as security monitoring or technical support.

examples.en: The hospital provides around-the-clock care for its patients.
examples.cn: 医院为患者提供全天候护理。

examples.en: The tech team is working around-the-clock to fix the server issues.
examples.cn: 技术团队正在全天候工作以修复服务器问题。

examples.en: The police have been monitoring the area around-the-clock after the incident.
examples.cn: 事件发生后，警察一直在该地区进行全天候监控。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于描述某种活动或服务不间断地持续进行，通常用于表示某种努力、监控或服务在一天的所有时间段里都在进行。它通常应用于紧急情况、医疗服务或者需要全天候关注的场合，如安全监控或者技术支持。

definition.cn: “忙得像蜜蜂” 或 “非常忙碌”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the behavior of bees. Bees are considered very industrious insects because they constantly collect nectar and pollen to sustain the hive. Therefore, describing someone as "busy as a bee" implies that the person works very hard and is always occupied.

examples.en: She's always as busy as a bee with her multiple jobs.
examples.cn: 她总是因为她的多份工作忙得像蜜蜂。

examples.en: During the holidays, he becomes as busy as a bee preparing everything.
examples.cn: 在假期期间，他忙着准备一切，忙得像蜜蜂。

examples.en: She was as busy as a bee organizing the event.
examples.cn: 她在组织活动的时候忙得像蜜蜂一样。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自蜜蜂的行为习性。蜜蜂被认为是非常勤劳的昆虫，因为它们不停地采集花蜜和花粉，以维持蜂群的生存。因此，形容一个人 “忙得像蜜蜂” 意味着他（她）工作很勤奋，总是忙碌不停。

definition.cn: “像 ABC 一样简单”，表示某事非常简单、易于理解或完成。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the very basic English education, starting with the alphabet ABC, considered the initial and simplest knowledge. Over time, "As easy as ABC" has become a common expression to indicate that a process or task is very easy.

examples.en: Learning how to use this phone is as easy as ABC.
examples.cn: 学习使用这款手机非常简单，像 ABC 一样容易。

examples.en: Solving this puzzle was as easy as ABC.
examples.cn: 解这个谜题如同 ABC 一样简单。

examples.en: Setting up the new printer was as easy as ABC.
examples.cn: 安装新的打印机非常简单，像 ABC 一样轻松。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于最基本的英文教育，从字母表的 ABC 开始教学，因此被认为是最初和最简单的知识。随着时间的推移，“As easy as ABC” 成为了一种常见的表达，用以说明某个过程或任务非常容易。

definition.cn: “轻而易举” 或 “无比简单”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in 19th century America, where baking a pie was considered a simple and enjoyable task. Combining the sweet and simple nature of pie-making, “as easy as pie” came to describe something very easy and effortless to do.

examples.en: The math problem was as easy as pie.
examples.cn: 这道数学题轻而易举。

examples.en: Fixing the computer was as easy as pie for her.
examples.cn: 修理电脑对她来说简直轻而易举。

examples.en: He said the test was as easy as pie.
examples.cn: 他说考试简直轻而易举。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于19世纪的美国，当时做派通常被认为是简单而令人愉快的事情。与做派的甜美和简单制作过程相结合，“as easy as pie” 就被用来形容某事非常简单，无需费力。

title: As genuine as a three-dollar bill

definition.cn: “假到不行” 或 “完全不是真的”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the fact that there is no genuine three-dollar bill in the United States. Therefore, any supposed three-dollar bill must be a counterfeit. Hence, the phrase is commonly used to describe something or someone as completely untrustworthy or fake.

examples.en: His apology was as genuine as a three-dollar bill.
examples.cn: 他的道歉和三美元钞票一样假。

examples.en: That offer sounds as genuine as a three-dollar bill.
examples.cn: 那个报价听起来和三美元钞票一样不可信。

examples.en: Her compliments are as genuine as a three-dollar bill.
examples.cn: 她的赞美和三美元钞票一样虚伪。

origin.cn: 这个短语的出处在于美国没有真正的三美元纸币，因此，任何所谓的三美元纸币必然是假币。所以，当需要形容某事物或者某个人完全不可信不真实时，人们会使用这个短语。

definition.cn: “心满意足” 或 “非常高兴”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the East Coast of the United States among fishermen. Clams are difficult to catch during high tide as they are safely buried in the sand. Hence, fishermen believed that clams are happiest during these moments safe from capture. Over time, the idiom evolved to describe someone who is very happy or content.

examples.en: After getting the promotion, he was as happy as a clam.
examples.cn: 获得晋升后，他心满意足。

examples.en: She felt as happy as a clam while lying on the beach all day.
examples.cn: 她一整天躺在海滩上，感到非常高兴。

examples.en: The kids were as happy as clams playing in the park.
examples.cn: 孩子们在公园里玩得非常高兴。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于美国东海岸的渔民。蛤蜊在涨潮时很难被捕捉到，这时它们可以安全地躲在沙泥中。因此，渔民认为此时的蛤蜊是最快乐的，因为它们能够安全地避开捕捉。这句惯用语逐渐延伸用来形容人非常高兴或者心满意足的状态。

definition.cn: “像老鼠一样安静” 或 “非常安静”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the behavior of mice, which are known to be very quiet and stealthy when they move around. Therefore, "as quiet as a mouse" is used to describe someone or something that is extremely quiet or does not make any noise. This phrase is often used to illustrate a person's very silent or diminutive presence.

examples.en: The children were as quiet as a mouse during the movie.
examples.cn: 孩子们在看电影时像老鼠一样安静。

examples.en: She was as quiet as a mouse when sneaking into the kitchen for a midnight snack.
examples.cn: 她偷偷摸摸去厨房吃夜宵时，像老鼠一样安静。

examples.en: Despite the chaos around him, he remained as quiet as a mouse.
examples.cn: 尽管周围一片混乱，他依然像老鼠一样安静。

origin.cn: 这个成语的起源是因为老鼠在我们周围活动时常常是极为安静、悄无声息的。因此，“as quiet as a mouse” 用来形容一个人或环境非常安静，不发出任何声音。这个短语通常用来描述某人的行为极为安静或微不足道的状态。

definition.cn: “稀有罕见” 或 “非常稀有”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the fact that hens do not have teeth. Therefore, this expression is used to describe something that is extremely rare or nearly impossible to find. It humorously emphasizes the extreme rarity of an object or situation.

examples.en: Opportunities like this are as rare as hen's teeth.
examples.cn: 像这样的机会简直稀有得像鸡的牙齿。

examples.en: Honest politicians are as rare as hen's teeth these days.
examples.cn: 如今，诚实的政客稀有得像鸡的牙齿。

examples.en: In this region, rain during summer is as rare as hen's teeth.
examples.cn: 在这个地区，夏天的雨水稀有得像鸡的牙齿。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于一个事实，即鸡是没有牙齿的。所以，用这个短语来描述某事物极其稀有，几乎不可能找到。它像笑话一样强调了物体或情况的极端罕见性。

definition.cn: “完好无损” 或 “非常健康”。
definition.en: This phrase's origin is not entirely clear, but it is believed to be related to the beneficial effects of rain in nature, particularly in agriculture where rain is essential for crop growth. Thus, "as right as rain" means that something or someone is in optimal condition, unharmed, or has recovered health.

examples.en: After a few days of rest, I'm feeling as right as rain.
examples.cn: 休息了几天之后，我感觉非常健康。

examples.en: The mechanic fixed the car, and now it's as right as rain.
examples.cn: 修理工修好了车，现在它完好无损了。

examples.en: Don’t worry, everything will be as right as rain by tomorrow.
examples.cn: 别担心，一切明天就会恢复正常。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源不完全确定，但据认为它与 “雨” 在自然界带来的有利影响有关，尤其是在农业中，雨水是作物生长所必需的。因此，“as right as rain” 表示某物或某人处于最佳状态，完好无损，或恢复了健康。

definition.cn: “直线距离” 或 “两点之间的最短距离”。
definition.en: This phrase is believed to originate from the observation that crows fly in a straight line. When crows fly, they often take the most direct path because it is the least strenuous. Therefore, this idiom is used to describe the shortest distance between two points, disregarding any twists and turns of roads or terrain.

examples.en: The village is about 10 miles away as the crow flies.
examples.cn: 村庄距离这里大约 10 英里（直线距离）。

examples.en: It's only a few blocks as the crow flies, but a much longer walk due to the winding streets.
examples.cn: 按照直线距离只有几个街区，但由于道路曲折，步行要长很多。

examples.en: As the crow flies, the airport is quite close, but it takes an hour to get there by car.
examples.cn: 按照直线距离，机场很近，但开车则要一个小时。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源据说与乌鸦会沿直线飞行有关。乌鸦在飞行时会选择直线路线，因为这是最省力的方式。因此，这个成语用来形容两点之间的最短距离，不考虑道路或地形的曲折。

title: As white as a sheet/as white as a ghost

definition.cn: “脸色苍白” 或 “面无血色”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the comparison of someone's face turning very pale due to fear, illness, or shock, likening it to the whiteness of a sheet or a ghost. It is commonly used to describe someone who looks bloodless for some reason.

examples.en: When she heard the news, she turned as white as a sheet.
examples.cn: 听到这个消息，她脸色变得苍白。

examples.en: He looked as white as a ghost after walking out of the haunted house.
examples.cn: 从鬼屋出来后，他看起来面无血色。

examples.en: The sudden fright made him go as white as a sheet.
examples.cn: 突如其来的惊吓让他的脸色变得苍白。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自形容一个人因惊吓、病痛或惊讶而脸色变得非常苍白，就像一张白纸或幽灵一样。通常用来描述因为某种原因而丧失血色的情况。

definition.cn: “顶多” 或” 最好也不过是”。
definition.en: This phrase is used to indicate that something is at its optimal or best possible condition, although this condition still might be unsatisfactory or below expectations. It often carries a tone of dissatisfaction or disappointment.

examples.en: The weather will be cloudy at best this weekend.
examples.cn: 这个周末的天气顶多是阴天。

examples.en: At best, the project will be completed by next month.
examples.cn: 这个项目最早也要到下个月才能完成。

examples.en: His performance was mediocre at best.
examples.cn: 他的表现顶多也就是一般。

origin.cn: 这个短语用于表示某事物在最理想、最好的情况下也不过如此，可能与期望值有较大差距。通常这个短语会带有一种不满或失望的意味。

definition.cn: “至少”。
definition.en: This phrase is used to indicate the minimum amount or level of something. It emphasizes that even in the worst scenario, there will be a minimum outcome or situation. "At least" is a reassuring phrase used to point out the lowest standard or result.

examples.en: We were late, but at least we got to see the end of the movie.
examples.cn: 我们迟到了，但至少看到了电影的结尾。

examples.en: At least try to finish your homework before going out.
examples.cn: 至少在出门之前试着完成作业。

examples.en: It's cold, but at least it’s not raining.
examples.cn: 天气冷，但至少没下雨。

origin.cn: 这个短语用于表示某事物或情况的最低限度。它强调即使在最坏的情况下，也会有某个最低限度的结果或情况。“At least” 是一种保证性的话术，用来指出最低的标准或结果。

definition.cn: “意见不合” 或 “严重争执”。
definition.en: This idiom dates back to the 16th century, where "loggerheads" initially referred to a heavy tool used for stirring hot tar or molten lead. Given its weight, the tools would produce a loud clashing sound when collided. As a result, "at loggerheads" evolved to describe a state of severe conflict or disagreement between two or more parties.

examples.en: The two politicians have been at loggerheads over the new policy.
examples.cn: 这两位政客对新政策意见不合。

examples.en: My parents are always at loggerheads about money matters.
examples.cn: 我父母总是因金钱问题争执不断。

examples.en: The company and the union are at loggerheads over the new contract.
examples.cn: 公司和工会因新合同而严重争执。

origin.cn: 这个成语最早出现在16世纪，“loggerheads” 原意是一种厚重的劳动工具，用来搅拌沥青或是熔化铅等。由于工具粗重，两者撞击时会发出巨大的碰撞声，“at loggerheads” 因此演变成了形容两人或多方处于激烈冲突或争执的状态。

definition.cn: “束手无策” 或 “智穷技尽”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from Old English, where "wits" referred to someone's intellect or judgment. "At my wits' end" means that a person has exhausted all their intelligence and methods and still doesn't know what to do. It is often used to describe a state of feeling unable to continue when faced with a complex problem or predicament.

examples.en: After trying everything to get the project back on track, I'm at my wits' end.
examples.cn: 在尝试了所有方法让项目回归正轨后，我已经束手无策了。

examples.en: With the kids screaming and the dog barking, I was at my wits' end.
examples.cn: 孩子们尖叫，狗也在叫，我真的是智穷技尽了。

examples.en: She was at her wits' end trying to solve the puzzle.
examples.cn: 她在解这个谜题时已经无计可施了。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于古英语，"wits" 指的是一个人的智力或判断能力。"At my wits' end" 意味着一个人已经用尽所有的智慧和方法，仍然不知道该怎么办。通常用来描述在面对复杂问题或困境时感觉无法继续下去的一种状态。

title: At the bottom of the totem pole

definition.cn: “在图腾柱的底部” 或 “处于最低层级”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the Native American culture, where totem poles were carved to represent family, tribe, or personal insignias. The bottom carvings were often perceived as the lowest rank. "At the bottom of the totem pole" is used to signify someone being in the lowest rank or position in an organization or system.

examples.en: As a new intern, I started at the bottom of the totem pole.
examples.cn: 作为一个新实习生，我从图腾柱的底部开始工作。

examples.en: In this company, you need to work your way up from the bottom of the totem pole.
examples.cn: 在这家公司，你需要从图腾柱的底部一步步往上爬。

examples.en: I'm used to being at the bottom of the totem pole, but I'm working hard to get promoted.
examples.cn: 我习惯于处于图腾柱的底部，但我正在努力争取晋升。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于美洲土著文化中的图腾柱，图腾柱用雕刻动物或神灵的形象来代表家族、部落或个人的标志，底部的雕刻通常被认为是在等级中最低的位置。“at the bottom of the totem pole” 用来表示某人在组织或系统中的最低层级或最低地位。

definition.cn: “一大清早” 或 “破晓时分”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the first light of the day when the sun rises, typically indicating an extremely early time. In ancient times, many daily activities and work would start at dawn, so this phrase is used to describe an early time, indicating the beginning of an activity or work at the break of first light.

examples.en: They started their journey at the crack of dawn to avoid the heat.
examples.cn: 他们一大清早就开始了旅程，以避开酷热。

examples.en: I always walk my dog at the crack of dawn before heading to work.
examples.cn: 我总是在天刚亮的时候遛狗，然后再去上班。

examples.en: Farmers often wake up at the crack of dawn to tend to their fields.
examples.cn: 农民们通常在破晓时分起床去照料田地。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于破晓时太阳开始升起时发出的第一道光，通常意味着非常早的时间点。在古代，许多日常活动和工作都是从清晨开始的，因此，这个短语用来形容非常早的时间，表示在天刚亮的时候开始某项活动或工作。

title: At the drop of a hat

definition.cn: “立刻” 或 “毫不犹豫”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from old competitions or duels where the dropping of a hat would signal the start. Therefore, "at the drop of a hat" means to start immediately upon the hat dropping, with no hesitation. In modern English, this idiom is used to describe a person who will do something immediately and without hesitation.

examples.en: He would help his friends at the drop of a hat.
examples.cn: 他会毫不犹豫地帮助他的朋友。

examples.en: She is ready to travel at the drop of a hat.
examples.cn: 她随时准备出发旅行。

examples.en: Don't worry, I'll be there at the drop of a hat if you need me.
examples.cn: 别担心，如果你需要我，我会立刻赶到。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于以前的竞技比赛或决斗，裁判会丢下一顶帽子作为开始的信号。因此，“at the drop of a hat” 表示当帽子掉下时，行动立刻开始，没有任何延迟。在现代英语中，这个短语用来形容一个人会立刻做某些事情，毫不犹豫地去行动。

title: At the end of your rope

definition.cn: “走投无路” 或 “忍无可忍”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from farm work, referring to the point where a rope has reached its maximum length. It symbolizes someone having exhausted all means or patience. It is often used to convey extreme fatigue or helplessness.

examples.en: I'm really at the end of my rope with this project; nothing seems to work.
examples.cn: 我对这个项目真的走投无路了；没有什么方案有效。

examples.en: She was at the end of her rope, unable to find a solution to her problems.
examples.cn: 她已经忍无可忍，无法找到解决问题的方法。

examples.en: John is at the end of his rope with his job; he can't take it anymore.
examples.cn: 约翰对他的工作已经忍无可忍了；他再也受不了了。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自农场工作，用来表示一条绳子到了尽头。比喻某人已经使尽了最后的手段或忍耐到了极限。通常用于表达极度的疲劳或无助。
